7 Brew Sunrise 7 Fizz Soda: Price, Calories & Caffeine

A medium Sunrise 7 Fizz Soda is about $3.50, with 250 calories, 0 mg of caffeine and 64 g of sugar. Every number here comes from 7 Brew's own published nutrition guide, broken out by size and preparation.

Is there a sugar-free Sunrise 7 Fizz Soda?

Yes — 7 Brew lists a sugar-free version built with sugar-free syrups. Comparing mediums (iced):

VersionCaloriesSugarCarbsCaffeine
Sunrise 7 Fizz Soda25064 g65 g0 mg
Sugar-free Sunrise 7 Fizz Soda00 g0 g0 mg

Caffeine does not change — only the syrup does. See every sugar-free option in the customization guide.

Sunrise 7 Fizz Soda allergens

7 Brew's published allergen guide lists no declared allergens for the standard Sunrise 7 Fizz Soda. Adding a milk, syrup or topping changes this, and every drink is made on shared equipment, so cross-contact is possible.

If you are ordering around an allergy, check the full allergen and dietary guide and confirm at the window.

How to order a Sunrise 7 Fizz Soda

Ask for it by name — it is on the standard board at every 7 Brew, so no special script is needed. Say the size first, then the drink: "Can I get a medium Sunrise 7 Fizz Soda?"

Worth knowing before you order: the base is customisable. You can swap milk, ask for sugar-free syrups, change the sweetness level, or have most drinks made iced, hot or blended as a frozen chiller where the menu allows. Ordering through the app earns 100 rewards points either way.

Make a Sunrise Fizz at Home

Peach and raspberry over sparkling water. Two syrups, no orange anywhere near it.

For one medium fizz

  • 1/2 oz peach syrup
  • 1/2 oz raspberry syrup
  • 10 to 12 oz plain sparkling water
  • A full cup of ice
  • Optional: a spoon or two of coconut milk floated on top for the layered look
  1. Both syrups over the ice.
  2. Sparkling water in slow, one gentle stir.
  3. Coconut milk over the top last if you want the gradient. Drink it before it fully blends, or don't. Both are fine.

Sugar-free at home: sugar-free versions of both syrups rebuild the published sugar-free drink, a true zero in a medium. Energy version: same syrups over an energy drink base instead of sparkling water. That is the caffeinated twin, and it has its own page on this site.

7 Brew Sunrise 7 Fizz Soda FAQ

How many calories are in a 7 Brew Sunrise 7 Fizz Soda?

A medium iced Sunrise 7 Fizz Soda has 250 calories. A small has 170 and a large 340, according to 7 Brew's nutrition guide.

How much caffeine is in a 7 Brew Sunrise 7 Fizz Soda?

0 mg. This is the caffeine-free twin of the Sunrise energy drink.

How much does a 7 Brew Sunrise 7 Fizz Soda cost?

Roughly $2.75 for a small, $3.50 for a medium and $4.25 for a large. Prices are our estimates and vary by stand — every 7 Brew is independently owned.

How much sugar is in a 7 Brew Sunrise 7 Fizz Soda?

64 g in a medium, or 0 g if you order the sugar-free version.

Is there orange in a Sunrise Fizz?

No. Sunrise is peach and raspberry. That is the official combo, and it matters because one of the biggest data guides online says orange and peach, over and over, in an otherwise careful table. Orange lives in other drinks: Blood Orange is orange and pomegranate, Pixie Stick adds almond to that pair. If your Sunrise tastes like orange, something got built wrong.

What is the difference between Sunrise Fizz and Sunrise Energy?

Same two syrups, different base, and the searches blur them constantly. Google's own answer box calls the energy drink the most common Sunrise, which tells you where the crowd goes. The Sunrise 7 Energy has 105 mg of caffeine in a medium. This fizz has none, and costs less. Peach and raspberry either way. Say fizz or energy out loud when you order, because the names will not do the work for you.

Is the sugar-free Sunrise Fizz actually 0 calories?

Yes, as published. Sugar-Free Sunrise is a real entry in the official guide: 0 calories and 0 g of sugar in kids, small and medium, and 5 calories in a large. Only two named fizzes have a published sugar-free version, this one and Peaches 'n Cream. Odd detail: the top search result for this drink is a whole page about the sugar-free version, and it still estimates 5 to 10 calories for a medium instead of using the guide's 0, and never lists the regular drink's numbers at all. Both sets are on this page. The full sugar-free picture is on our sugar-free drinks page.

Why is Sunrise not on the main fizz board?

Good eye. The official fizz page features 10 drinks, and Sunrise is not one of them. It sits in the suggested flavor combos list underneath. But the nutrition guide gives it full entries, regular and sugar-free, which is more than some featured drinks get. It is a menu regular in everything but the poster. Order it by name.

How do fans get that layered sunrise look?

With a finish, not a trick pour. The layered cups in the fan groups are topped with coconut milk or a scoop of cream, which sits on the fizz and drifts down through it. The peach and raspberry underneath give the pink-to-gold fade. No syrup floating required, and the coconut plays nicer with peach than you would guess.
